reason: Checked and confirmed. READ TABLE row 1 (CONTEXT l.1991) ignores the error class. lb_poll.py l.4 parses the CLI 'submissions -v' CSV, which has no error column. kaggle 2.2.4's ApiSubmission does expose error_description, and the proposed one-liner ran fine read-only at 00:58Z (#37 and #38 PENDING, field ''). Both are still PENDING, so writing this now is an honest pre-score clarification: no knob, no new mechanism, no rule R1-R10 touched. The three branches hold up. (a) A 'Kaggle Error' is on Kaggle's side, so resubmitting K2 v1 repeats the pre-registered F1. Moving to K1 would drop lowrefine without the R3 evidence (d1 <= -0.002). (b) If K2 and the twin both time out or exceed compute, K1 shares safetail's 9.5 h repair deadline and the x138 runtime profile. K1 does lack lowrefine, a possible cause of the extra time, so it is not certain to fail. Still, holding K1 and asking the user is the conservative choice. (c) If only K2 throws, the difference from the twin is the insertion. #35 scored with the insertion, and safetail makes the insertion fail-soft, so K1 as written is right. Caveats: (1) we have never had an errored submission (1,359 poll.log lines, no ERROR), so it is unverified that error_description holds the class text; the Submissions page is the fallback. (2) Two cases are not assigned: a Timeout on K2 only with the twin COMPLETE, and a Kaggle Error on both. (3) Resubmitting K2 is a new LB slot and needs the user's OK. Value is small (P(K2 ERROR) ~0.02-0.03) but the cost is one CONTEXT paragraph, so it is worth adding.
fix: Add a dated pre-score clarification to CONTEXT (before any #37/#38 score appears in poll.log). ON K2 ERROR: (0) read the class with the one-liner (python -c "from kaggle.api.kaggle_api_extended import KaggleApi as K; a=K(); a.authenticate(); [print(s.ref, s.status, repr(s.error_description)) for s in a.competition_submissions('biohub-cell-tracking-during-development')[:4]]"). If error_description is empty, read the class on https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/biohub-cell-tracking-during-development/submissions (read-only). Then take the first matching case. (a) 'Kaggle Error' on K2 and the twin COMPLETE: resubmit K2 v1 unchanged in the next 26 Sep slot [OK]. It counts as K2 for the READ TABLE. A second Kaggle Error goes to (d). (b) 'Notebook Timeout' or 'Exceeded Allowed Compute' on BOTH K2 and the twin: no K1. Ask the user. F1/F2 follow the §f fallback order (item 4 = #34, then exp52). (c) 'Threw Exception', 'CSV Not Found' or 'Scoring/Format Error' on K2 only: row 1 as written (K1 = exp58t v1 [OK]). (d) Anything else (a Timeout or compute error on K2 only, a Kaggle Error on both, a mixed class, or an unreadable class): no automatic action. Ask the user; the default is row 1 [OK]. Optionally have lb_poll.py log error_description for ERROR rows (fail-soft, one extra read-only API call).
realistic_gain: Most likely 0: K2 errors with P ~0.02-0.03. In the 'Kaggle Error' case it keeps lowrefine in F1 and avoids a K1 that would change components on no evidence, a possible 0-0.001 public/private difference. In the both-timeout case it saves a slot and ~8 h on a K1 that would likely also fail, and gets the user's decision in earlier. The cost is one paragraph plus one read-only API call.
